alex: Heads-up — onboarding Odyssey-8B for evals. License language says "research-only" and there's a line about embeddings. Can we host embeddings for customers or is that a hard no?
tess: quick context — I ran int8 quant on our eval suite, quality is fine. Customers are already asking for embeddings/search.
maria: license excerpt i pasted below, read literally it looks restrictive:
```text
6. Use: Model may be used for non-commercial research and evaluation only.
9. Derivatives: Distribution of derivative model weights prohibited without permission.
Embeddings: Derived embeddings may be used for internal research but not hosted as a service.
```
sam: so two questions: 1) is hosting embeddings as an API "hosting as a service" (commercial)? 2) does quantized weights = derivative that we can't distribute?
tess: my read — hosting embeddings to paying customers is commercial activity. quantization probably produces a derivative weight set. both likely blocked unless we get permission.
claire-legal: short answer: risky. "Research-only" plus explicit embeddings line means public/paid hosting is not allowed. Quantization/packing that changes weights is a derivative under most licenses — distribution requires upstream permission.
claire-legal: options we can pursue: 1) request a commercial license / exception from upstream; 2) offer Private (customer-run) deployment where we don't redistribute weights; 3) recommend an alternate permissive model for hosted embeddings.
alex: if we do inference-only hosted API (no weights exposed), would that be ok? we already host many inference-only models.
claire-legal: inference-only still counts as "hosting" if the end customer uses it as a service and pays. For internal experiments or free research previews without commercial intent it's probably fine, but for paid product features it's not.
maria: quick pragmatic question — is a VPC/private Dedicated offering enough? customer runs in their VPC, we ship a container to them — does that avoid redistribution concerns?
claire-legal: yes — customer-managed infra where they accept the package/weights under terms is safer. We need to ensure the contract covers indemnity and confirms customer usage rights.
sam: i'll mark the onboarding ticket with license-blocker and list the three options (request commercial, private deployment, switch model).
legal-bot: Created support ticket: #ML-1229 — "Odyssey-8B license review / commercial exception request" (link: https://redwood.example.co/tickets/ML-1229)
ops-bot: created onboarding task in backlog: ONB-457 (tagged: license-blocker).
alex: thanks everyone. tagging for follow-up: @claire-legal can you draft the exception email template? i'll hold on rolling quantized artifact until we have clearance. :thumbsup:
claire-legal: yup — will draft and ping legal ops with next steps.
